Dark-diversity classification of species-region pairs

Source: R/aggregate.R
dn_dark.Rd

Applies the full conjunction rule of the source studies: a pair is climatically admissible if the calibrated establishment probability exceeds p_min and every supplied null screen has SES >= ses_min; it is dark if additionally the species is absent from the region.

Usage

dn_dark(pairs, p_min = 0.177, ses_cols = character(), ses_min = 2)

Arguments

pairs

data.frame with at least species, region, present (logical), a probability column p_establish, and one or more SES columns given in ses_cols.

p_min

admissibility threshold on the establishment probability. The source studies' externally calibrated value (Youden threshold of a species-blocked, climate-only model validated on documented introduced ranges) is 0.177; recalibrate with dn_calibrate() when using a different model or metric.

ses_cols

character vector of SES column names (e.g. c("n1_ses", "n2_ses", "n3_ses")).

ses_min

SES criterion (default 2).

Value

pairs with logical columns admissible and dark.

Examples

pairs <- data.frame(species = c("a", "a", "b"), region = c("r1", "r2", "r1"),
                    present = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
                    p_establish = c(0.6, 0.4, 0.05),
                    n2_ses = c(3.1, 2.5, 4.0))
dn_dark(pairs, ses_cols = "n2_ses")
#>   species region present p_establish n2_ses admissible  dark
#> 1       a     r1    TRUE        0.60    3.1       TRUE FALSE
#> 2       a     r2   FALSE        0.40    2.5       TRUE  TRUE
#> 3       b     r1   FALSE        0.05    4.0      FALSE FALSE
